summary: Kazi Dawa Samdup (1868–1922) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as headmaster at Maharaja's Bhutia Boarding School (~1906–1919) and teacher at the University of Calcutta (~1919–1922), teaching Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz and Herbert Bruce Hannah.
Kazu Uehara (1924–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyushu University (~1948–1953) and was appointed professor emeritus at Seijo University (~1995).

Kazuaki Komine (born 1947) specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Tokushima University (~1979–1990) and is attested as Professor Emeritus at Rikkyo University between 2015 and 2019.

Kazufumi Oki (born 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, completing doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He taught at Shuchiin University as assistant professor (attested 1982–1988) and later served as professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013), teaching Shinshu Kusumoto.

Kazuharu Mizuno (born 1958) studied at Nagoya University (BA, ~1978–1982), Hokkaido University (Master's, ~1982–1984), and Tokyo Metropolitan University (DSc, ~1984–1989). Around 2009, he served as a professor in the Department of Geography at Kyoto University.

Kazuhiko Yoshida (born 1955) works in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Sophia University, Kyoto University, and Cornell University (PhD, ~1982–1986) under Jay Jasanoff. He held posts at Nagoya City University (~1989–1996) and Kyoto University (professor, ~2000–2020).
Kazuhiro Furuta (born 1940) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as editor and publisher at the Otani Society (attested 1991) and as Dean at Otani University (attested 1998).
Kazuhiro Kawasaki (born 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral course at Koyasan University, where he also held a post as a researcher around 2005.
Kazuhiro Yamamoto specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Silpakorn University (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya.

Kazunobu Matsuda is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University (attested 1979) and later lectured there (attested 1985–1989). He served as a professor at Bukkyo University (2009) and Kyoto University (attested 2005).

Kazuo Hyodo (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe, earning his PhD. He later served as assistant professor at Otani University (~1983–2014) and committee member at the Otani Society.

Kazuo Kano (born 1974) studied at Kyoto University under Katsumi Mimaki and the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Klaus-Dieter Mathes. He held posts at Hamburg, Kyoto University, Koyasan University (professor, ~2008–2017), and Komazawa University.
Kazuo Okabe (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University (~1954–1958), later serving there as a professor (~1978–2006) and teaching Jamie Hubbard.

Kazuo Osumi (1932–2024) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955) in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Hokkaido University (~1971–1980) and served as professor at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (~1980–2001).
Kazuo Oyamada (born 1952) works in Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. He studied at Tamagawa University and held a post at Rissho University.

Kazuyoshi Hotta focuses on Indology and Buddhist studies, pursuing doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo and serving as manager of its Young Buddhist Association (attested 2007). He later served as fixed-term assistant professor at Otani University (attested 2015).

Kazuyoshi Kino (1922–2013) studied at Shudo Junior & Senior High School and the University of Tokyo (~1945–1948) in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held academic posts at Shogen Junior College and Hosen Gakuen College.
Kazuyoshi Soma (born 1942) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Meiji Yamada. He held a post as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).
Keenan W. Cox specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He pursued an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2014).

Kees W. Bolle (1927–2012) studied at Leiden University (~1948–1953) in religious studies and Indology. He was a fellow at the Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study and Professor Emeritus of History at the University of California, Los Angeles (attested 2005).
